gen-righteous-gf-inter-tight: Righteous bends thin steel rod into fat, line-filling bowls, a heading with real swagger. Inter Tight lines up underneath like tubing, its short ascenders keeping quiet.
gen-righteous-gf-karla: Playful and bold in the heading, this pair has a pencil-line consistency up top that the body can lean against. Karla follows with a tall middle band and a gaping c, stocky and friendly.
gen-righteous-gf-kedebideri: Friendly is the first word for this pair: Righteous holds its width through every turn, while Kedebideri rises on a skyward x-height with rounded, inviting letters. Together they are bold yet approachable.
gen-righteous-gf-khula: Fun runs through the heading, where Righteous bends each letter from a single length of wire. Khula sits beside it with a tall, brush-pen belly and curves that keep their mouths open.
gen-righteous-gf-krub: Krub brings a pronounced x-height and curves that lift off before the loop closes. Righteous, bent from rod with no thick-and-thin shift at all, gives it a loud partner to sit under.
gen-righteous-gf-kufam: Neon-tube lettering, basically: Kufam keeps one track width, with generous open curves in e and ascenders that hardly show. Righteous above it fills the line with big bowls and steel-rod bends.
gen-righteous-gf-lexend: Righteous fills each line with bowls bent from thin steel rod, a heading with plenty of command. And Lexend answers underneath with outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve.
gen-righteous-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca draws a plain, unshaded line whose terminals stop short of curling back. Its capitals look small beside the big lowercase, so you can adjust its size freely while Righteous stays put.
gen-righteous-gf-liter: Modern in feel, this pair sets Righteous's bowls and bent steel rod against tall lowercase. Liter has stroke contrast of exactly none, and wide mouths on its round forms.
gen-righteous-gf-mada: Straight-edged, constant strokes and bowls that fill the line give Righteous its commanding look. Mada follows with a towering midzone and curves that refuse to close, loosening the page.
